we identified perturbative interventions that can selectively inhibit signaling hubs in a stimulus-specific manner.
we identified principles that delineate how to target dynamic signaling to achieve therapeutic specificity.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of cellular signaling.
the development of mathematical methods to understand the dynamics of signaling networks and to use these methods to identify new therapeutic targets.
the dynamics of signaling and the role it plays in the specificity of cellular responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dynamics of signalling may serve as a target for pharmacological intervention, and that we have revealed principles that delineate both the opportunities and constraints for developing stimulus-specific therapeutic drugs aimed at pleiotropically acting signalling hubs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we can identify the dynamics of signaling as a pharmacological targets, and that there are opportunities and constraints of stimulus-specific therapeutic agents that are aimed at pleiotrophic signaling hubs.
we have identified principles that may guide the design of therapeutic agents that target the dynamics of pleiotropic signaling modules.
the dynamics of a signaling pathway can be targeted pharmacologically, even when the signaling hub is pleiotropic and highly networked.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dynamic features of signaling may be targeted pharmacologicaly to achieve therapeutic specificity.
the dynamics of signal propagation may serve as a target for pharmacological intervention.
the dynamics of the signal can be exploited as a pharmacological lever to achieve therapeutic specificity, even when the underlying molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
